analytical_question: Can both shifts operate a four-week shadow pilot now, and can the retailer sustain routine use?
general_et_finding: An item tag can identify an individual garment during a count; the GS1 case establishes deployment precedent, not local accuracy.
application_finding: Comparing a shadow count of denim with manual recounts can expose stock discrepancies. A tag read alone cannot establish which stock record needs correction.
organization_specific_finding: Sponsorship supported: four-week sponsor commitment. Skills supported for counting: two leads passed exercise. Workflow supported: signed handoff and completed drill across shifts. Infrastructure/data supported for scope: reader, verified tag mapping and barcode fallback. Resources mixed: pilot funded; operating budget ends at week four. Governance supported for corrections: controller approval and no scan writeback. Culture/change partially supported: one reported mismatch without penalty, too little to infer store-wide trust. Operating ownership supported for pilot: closing lead, deputy, reserved time and controller escalation.

evidence.claim: I.T.’S. international used individually tagged garments for inventory counts in apparel stores.
evidence.date_or_recency: GS1 Japan case study, 2012; reviewed November 8, 2026.
evidence.notes: Establishes precedent; no transfer of time savings or present staffing readiness.

evidence.claim: Sponsor funds four weeks of one-store shadow counts. Two shift leads passed a count exercise; staff logged a mismatch without penalty. Stockroom has a reader, verified tag-to-SKU list and barcode recount procedure. Inventory Controller approves ledger corrections after recount; scans cannot write to the ledger. One named floor lead plus a trained deputy can collect counts. Both shifts have reserved count time. A signed roster gives the closing lead and deputy queue coverage, recount time and escalation to the controller before any correction. Both shifts completed a handoff drill. No ongoing budget beyond week four.
evidence.notes: Accepted for the exercise; not audited employer records.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Training and protected count time support a trial but do not establish sustained ownership. The case does not establish value or routine readiness.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the scoped judgment given the case facts; actual execution is unverified.
value_opportunity_implication: Count fully reconciled size/color discrepancies and total staff time, including exception work. Fast scanning alone cannot show operational value.
risk_governance_implication: Keep scans read-only. Escalate unresolved records rather than silently adjusting stock; controller retains correction authority.
recommendation_management_implication: Ready for a four-week shadow pilot only. Store lead should run the weekly count and log discrepancies through closure. Controller should compare exceptions with manual recounts. Sponsor must review workload and approve recurring staff time and funding before renewal.
change_monitoring_triggers: Pause on any unapproved ledger write or discrepancy that nobody accepts at shift handoff. Reassess at week four.
At week four review unresolved cases by shift, recount labor and recurring ownership; send value and adoption tradeoffs to the Adoption Agent.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Routine use is not ready. Ask the sponsor for a recurring budget and signed staffing plan.
